channel.title: RIEP Project Updates
channel.description: Coverage, public records and tools from the Rhode Island Elections Project.

item.title: New Cranston activity ranking and clearer council profiles
item.description:
RIEP has added a provisional Legislative Activity Index for the nine members who served on Cranston’s City Council in 2026. Each named sponsor receives full credit: 1 point for symbolic and advocacy measures, 2 for routine property or administrative approvals, and 5 for substantive local policy, fiscal measures and ordinances. Additional explicit cosponsorships are listed separately.
Profiles for six members of the 2026 council now show their activity rank and points, with the comparison to the council average combined into one clear summary. Daniel Wall and Frank Ritz are tied for first with 29 points each—53.5% above the council average. Wall’s profile also includes a newly added portrait. Incoming members are labeled “Not applicable” for 2026 and do not inherit their predecessors’ records.
The ranking links to measure-by-measure source records, topic tags, scoring explanations and downloadable data. It covers 42 identified measures across 19 available full-council meeting records. This is a partial record of documented sponsorship activity, not a finding of overall legislative effectiveness. Visitors can inspect the evidence and explore alternative scoring assumptions.

item.title: A new home for RIEP announcements and color-coded map choices
item.description:
RIEP has launched this project-updates archive to make new coverage and website changes easier to follow. Each notice includes a publication date and time, a permanent link and links to the relevant tools.
The homepage’s scrolling updates now link directly to these notices. The map chooser uses four distinct solid colors for current statewide results, historical maps, Cranston wards and the Providence pilot.

item.title: The Womxn Project’s BFFI ratings added to Cranston council profiles
item.description:
RIEP’s nine Cranston council profiles now display The Womxn Project’s 2026 Bodily Freedom Forever Index categories, with links to the publisher’s Cranston listing and information about the rating.
Green identifies “For,” red identifies “Against,” and gray identifies “N/A.” N/A means insufficient information, not opposition. These are outside issue ratings, displayed separately from organizational endorsements and RIEP’s own research.

item.title: Cranston council votes, attendance and election history are easier to explore
item.description:
Available 2026 full-council minutes now support member-specific vote records and opening roll-call attendance percentages. The archive links back to source records and keeps unresolved cases visible.
Attendance percentages exclude missing minutes and unresolved opening records; they do not establish presence throughout a meeting. Incoming members do not inherit a predecessor’s record. Profile election histories also include 2026 returns and verified 2024 ward results for five individuals.

item.title: Profiles now cover Cranston’s six ward and three citywide council winners
item.description:
RIEP’s municipal coverage includes all nine winners of Cranston’s 2026 City Council elections: six ward seats and three citywide seats. Profiles bring together sourced background information, available priorities, election returns and public records.
The Cranston map links local election returns with council profiles. Available campaign finance filings are linked from the relevant profiles. Current service is distinguished from the incoming council term beginning January 4, 2027.

item.title: Find Cranston and Providence ward maps from the homepage
item.description:
The “See Rhode Island Election Maps” button now opens a directory of statewide and local maps. Visitors can choose 2026 legislative returns, historical statewide views, Cranston’s ward map or the Providence council mapping pilot.
Providence remains pilot coverage. Local maps and profiles will expand as boundaries, official records and election information are verified.
